notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Filip Chytil is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Jacob Quillan was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Linus Karlsson and Liam Öhgren.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 4% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 2 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Alex Iafallo takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Tyrel Bauer is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Fleury and Salomonsson.

Josh Morrissey is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Mario Ferraro has taken his spot beside Dylan DeMelo. That pair has had 47% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 89:53 together, down from 61% with Morrissey.
Nico Daws joined from NJD on Oct 24.
Dawson Mercer joined from NJD on Oct 24 and has played beside Kyle Connor and Viggo Björck.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.
Elias Salomonsson has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 5 games, up from 8% last season.

story.head: Something has to change for the Jets
paras: The Jets are winless in nine (0-7-2), and the Canucks (3-12-1) lost 4-2 to Toronto on Saturday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Jets seventh in the Central (tied for 27th in the NHL).

The Canucks have played better than their record (.219) says: their chances are worth about .311, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Jets (.367 on chances worth .433), where their finishing has held them back.

The Canucks pick their shots (lowest), have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.50 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Jets, they create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely ice the puck (4th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (30th), so the Canucks have the edge over them on shot quality. Winnipeg has scored 2.27 goals a game, the third fewest in the league.

Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki (6 G / 7 A / 13 P in 16 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with five goals in eight games against Vancouver since 2023-24. Mark Scheifele (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 15 GP) isn’t far behind.
Leevi Meriläinen (2-5-1 / .897 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Vancouver, and Stuart Skinner (3-4-3 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) for Winnipeg.
